question: Infer differentiation trajectories from single-cell RNA-seq data and visualize the trajectory graph overlaid on a UMAP colored by cell cluster.

files.eval_guideline: Plot must show a UMAP with cells colored by cluster and at least one trajectory path overlaid; exact trajectory topology, color palette, and point size may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The files have the identical basename and PNG image format, and both correspond to the requested trajectory visualization overlaid on a cluster-colored UMAP.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic visual features—a UMAP with cluster-colored cells and at least one overlaid trajectory—while explicitly allowing differences in topology and styling. A semantic image comparison is therefore appropriate.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images fulfill the requested scientific visualization: each shows a UMAP embedding of single-cell RNA-seq data with cells colored by cluster and an inferred differentiation trajectory graph overlaid. The reference uses dark, mostly continuous curved paths across several colored cell populations, with cluster numbers placed near the populations. The candidate uses a PAGA maximum-connectivity spanning tree with directed black arrows, additional dashed edges, labeled cluster-median nodes, and a detailed legend containing cell-type annotations, cell counts, and median DPT values. The candidate therefore communicates trajectory direction and cluster identities more explicitly. There are substantial visual differences in the UMAP geometry, number and numbering of clusters, coordinate ranges, and trajectory topology; the reference appears to contain roughly nine displayed cluster labels, whereas the candidate contains thirteen clusters and includes isolated microglia. The reference trajectories also trace local structure within dense clusters, while the candidate primarily connects cluster centroids with straight graph edges. These differences could affect detailed biological interpretation, but the evaluation permits differences in exact topology and styling, and both convey the same core scientific message of cluster-resolved differentiation paths on a UMAP. No critical required element is missing.
